page_title: Tokenized Money Market Funds — Digital Assets Dashboard
page_subtitle_html: Tokenized money market fund (MMF) exposure aggregated from RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt. Networks and platforms are built from each fund's on-chain token deployments; Distributed Value columns are current levels.
kpi_window_note: Distributed value uses a 30-day (30D) % change vs summed token values 30 days ago. Top network share is the largest network by distributed value; the 30D figure is the change in market-share percentage points (pp), not a percent of total. Fund universe: fixed curated TMMF population on RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt; KPIs, charts, and league tables use the same fund set.
key_observations_html:
Key observations

  • TMMF distributed value fell 5.6% over 30D: With distributed value at $13.61B (5.6% lower over 30D), tokenized-cash balances look lighter—suggesting some institutions pulled liquidity or rotated away from TMMF wrappers even if headline product news stayed busy.
  • A global regulatory arbitrage map is emerging: distributed value clusters into distinct compliance regimes—U.S. Reg D ~35% of population AUM (e.g. BUIDL, iBENJI); U.S. Reg S ~35% of population AUM (e.g. USYC, USDY); U.S. mutual fund (N-1A) ~9% of population AUM (e.g. WTGXX, FILQ-A). Issuers appear to anchor products in familiar safe harbors rather than one global standard. Related: Mastercard and BVNK Launch 'Global Money Platform' to Merge Fiat and Stablecoins (Decrypt).
  • Multi-chain footprints are a distribution signal: Funds listing many networks with thin holder counts usually signal jurisdictional or distribution reach, not deep secondary liquidity on every chain. Related: Stripe and Plasma to Develop Multi-Currency Stablecoin Cards (The Defiant).
  • Issuer strategies are splitting into two models: Institutional cash rail programs (low holder counts, large AUM per holder—e.g. USYC, BUIDL, iBENJI, JLTXX) vs global yield / distribution products (broader holder bases, retail- or UCITS-friendly framing—e.g. USDY, WTGXX, BENJI, USTBL). These behave like different businesses under the same "tokenized MMF" label. Related: AI agents make 138 million crypto payments as U.S. dominates spending on AI models (CoinDesk).

Context only—not investment advice. Observations rank fund-level and network aggregates on this page against recent tokenization and money-market headlines. Bullets combine on-page data with recent industry headlines.

Key observations are AI generated and should be reviewed for accuracy.
